title: Cochain sections comparisons for arbitrary coefficient-ring towers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to its module universe, with terminal object $s$. Let $R_0\to R_1\to R_2\to R_3$ be a tower of sheaves of commutative rings and $A_0\to A_1\to A_2\to A_3$ a tower of commutative rings. Fix ring maps $\lambda_i:A_i\to\Gamma(s,R_i)$ commuting with every tower map. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheafified tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and unbounded cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Write $G_i(C)=\Gamma(s,C)$ termwise, regarded as an $A_i$-complex through $\lambda_i$, $T_{ij}C=C\otimes_{R_i}R_j$, and $t_{ij}N=N\otimes_{A_i}A_j$, for $i\le j$, with diagonal coefficient maps the identities. For all these pairs define the balanced sections comparison
$$\theta_{ij,C}:t_{ij}G_i(C)\longrightarrow G_j(T_{ij}C),\qquad n\otimes a\longmapsto n\otimes\lambda_j(a).$$
Let $u_{ijk,C}:T_{jk}T_{ij}C\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{ik}C$ denote the balanced sheaf scalar associator, with local formulas $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto x\otimes ab$ and inverse $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b$. Let $a_{ijk}$ be the identical scalar associator for ordinary module complexes, and let $m_i:T_{ii}C\to C$ and $\mu_i:t_{ii}N\to N$ be the action maps $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$ and $n\otimes a\mapsto an$.

The displayed balanced maps are well-defined natural chain maps, and $u$, $a$, $m$ and $\mu$ are natural chain isomorphisms with the indicated associator inverses and with unit inverses given by insertion of $1$. For every $i\le j\le k$ and every $R_i$-complex $C$,
$$G_k(u_{ijk,C})\circ\theta_{jk,T_{ij}C}\circ t_{jk}(\theta_{ij,C})=\theta_{ik,C}\circ a_{ijk,G_i(C)}.$$
Both sides send $((n\otimes a)\otimes b)$ to $n\otimes\lambda_k(ab)$. For every $i$,
$$G_i(m_i)\circ\theta_{ii,C}=\mu_i.$$
For the four-stage tower,
$$u_{023,C}\circ T_{23}(u_{012,C})=u_{013,C}\circ u_{123,T_{01}C}.$$
The corresponding module associators obey the same equation. Every composite of the three sections comparisons and these associators from $t_{23}t_{12}t_{01}G_0(C)$ to $G_3(T_{03}C)$ agrees; it sends $(((n\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c)$ to $n\otimes\lambda_3(abc)$. These equations are natural for all chain maps, including repeated stages and zero complexes. No exactness of $G_i$ or scalar extension, and no invertibility of $\theta$, is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the extension functor using the existing changeOfRingsPresheaf on objects, sectionwise ModuleCat.extendScalars on maps, and PresheafOfModules.sheafification. Its object and map equations are definitionally the prescribed changeOfRings and changeOfRingsHom. Use the ordinary extension/restriction Hom equivalence sectionwise, checking restriction compatibility on 1 tensor x, followed by the module sheafification adjunction [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. This works with independent site and coefficient universes, whereas the specialized ringed-tensor calculus uses a common universe. Maps out of the sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] are determined by the images of 1 tensor x over every site object. Restricting the codomain scalars and composing insertion maps gives the corresponding double and triple insertion extensionality statements. These are tests of sheaf morphisms, never assertions that global pure tensors generate all global sections.

proof.text: The map $n\otimes a\mapsto n\otimes\lambda_j(a)$ defining $\theta_{ij,M}$ is additive in both inputs and balanced over $A_i$: for $c\in A_i$, $(\lambda_i(c)n)\otimes\lambda_j(a)=n\otimes f_{ij}(\lambda_i(c))\lambda_j(a)=n\otimes\lambda_j(h_{ij}(c)a)$. Thus the ordinary tensor presentation gives an $A_j$-linear map. Here the sheaf pure tensor is the sheafification-unit image specified by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], evaluated at $s$. For a module map $v$, both routes of the naturality square send $n\otimes a$ to $v(n)\otimes\lambda_j(a)$; ordinary tensors generate its source. This constructs the comparison without assuming that its target is generated by global pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules. Agent-written balanced calculations.

proof.text: Use step 1 to extend the insertion $M\to\operatorname{Res}_{ij}T_{ik}M$ first along $f_{ij}$, then along $f_{jk}$. The resulting $R_k$-linear map $u:T_{jk}T_{ij}M\to T_{ik}M$ sends $(x\otimes r)\otimes t$ to $x\otimes f_{jk}(r)t$. In the other direction extend the double insertion $M\to\operatorname{Res}_{ik}T_{jk}T_{ij}M$ along $f_{ik}$, giving $v(x\otimes t)=(x\otimes1)\otimes t$. These insertions are linear over the required restricted rings since $f_{ik}=f_{jk}f_{ij}$. The composites $uv$ and $vu$ fix the single and double insertions respectively, so step 1 gives $uv=1$ and $vu=1$. Naturality follows by testing the same insertions: both routes for a map $M\to M'$ send $x$ to the insertion of its image.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules. Agent-written balanced calculations.

proof.text: The action $m_i:T_{ii}M\to M$ is the extension, under the adjunction of step 1, of $1_M$. It sends $x\otimes r$ to $rx$. Its inverse is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, which is $R_i$-linear because the coefficient map is the identity. One composite fixes $x$; the other fixes the insertion, hence is the identity by step 1. This also proves naturality. For ordinary modules the balanced tensor presentation gives exactly the same constructions of $a_{ijk}$ and $\mu_i$, with inverses inserting $1$; the two composite formulas reduce to $(na)\otimes b=n\otimes h_{jk}(a)b$ and $n\otimes a=a(n\otimes1)$. In Lean the ordinary scalar associator is constructed from TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange, and the ordinary identity action from TensorProduct.lid. Their values and inverses on tensors follow from these linear equivalences.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules. Agent-written balanced calculations.

proof.text: Apply these module maps in each degree of a cochain complex. All tensor differentials are $x\otimes r\mapsto dx\otimes r$, so $d^2=0$. Each naturality square already proved, applied to a differential, is the chain-map equation of [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. In particular $d\theta(n\otimes a)=dn\otimes\lambda_j(a)=\theta(dn\otimes a)$. The inverse maps of steps 3 and 4 also commute with $d$, so the resulting maps are chain isomorphisms. Applying the degreewise naturality equations to each component of an arbitrary chain map proves their naturality on complexes. The private module construction passes its concrete maps and proved laws directly to the combining argument; Mathlib termwise natural transformations and isomorphisms give the cochain maps without extra composition transports.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules. Agent-written balanced calculations.

proof.text: For $i\le j\le k$, evaluate the two sides of the comparison equation on $((n\otimes a)\otimes b)$ in each degree. The left route gives $(n\otimes\lambda_j(a))\otimes\lambda_k(b)$, then $n\otimes f_{jk}(\lambda_j(a))\lambda_k(b)$. The right route gives $n\otimes\lambda_k(h_{jk}(a)b)$. These agree by compatibility of $\lambda$ with the tower and multiplicativity of $\lambda_k$. Such double ordinary tensors generate the source, proving the equation. For the unit equation both routes on $n\otimes a$ give $\lambda_i(a)n=an$, with the last equality the defined $A_i$-action. Again ordinary tensor generation gives equality.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules. Agent-written balanced calculations.

proof.text: For the sheaf four-stage equation, apply the adjunction of step 1 three times. Both routes have domain $T_{23}T_{12}T_{01}M$ and codomain $T_{03}M$; they agree on the triple insertion, since each sends $x$ to $x\otimes1$. Thus they are equal. On an arbitrary iterated local pure tensor both send $(((x\otimes r)\otimes t)\otimes v)$ to $x\otimes f_{13}(r)f_{23}(t)v$, by step 3 and multiplicativity of the ring maps. The ordinary-module equation follows from the same computation on generating ordinary triple tensors, replacing $f$ by $h$. Apply this in each degree.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules. Agent-written balanced calculations.

proof.text: Finally, starting with $(((n\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c)$, any application of a binary sections comparison replaces a coefficient by its $\lambda$-image, and any associator multiplies adjacent coefficients after mapping them to the last ring. Steps 6 and 7 permit either binary grouping and either sheaf reassociation. Equivalently, direct substitution gives the common image $n\otimes\lambda_3(h_{13}(a)h_{23}(b)c)$ for every route from $t_{23}t_{12}t_{01}G_0(C)$ to $G_3(T_{03}C)$. Ordinary triple tensors generate this source in every degree. This proves the last coherence clause, with $abc$ in the statement understood through the tower maps. Every calculation also applies when stages repeat, when an input or a complex is zero, or when a coefficient ring is the zero ring: it uses only additive and unital multiplicative identities, with no cancellation, exactness or inverse for $\theta$. The equality of the five displayed routes is a categorical argument using naturality of theta, the binary comparison equation, and the sheaf four-stage equation. The common tensor value is computed for the final route using the ordinary scalar associators and then the sections comparison. In Lean apply the abstract route equality to the component in each degree, using module-level compatibility and four-stage equations, then use the two ordinary associator formulas and the comparison formula for the common tensor value.
